one_liner: LLVM/Clang-based C++ to WebAssembly and JavaScript compiler; vendor claims slightly smaller output than Emscripten at roughly equal speed.
what_it_does: Cheerp compiles C/C++ to a WebAssembly module plus JavaScript glue (default -target cheerp-wasm), to pure JavaScript (-target cheerp) or to WASI-only WebAssembly (-target cheerp-wasm-wasi), driven through its own clang/clang++ in /opt/cheerp. Its distinguishing feature is interop: code tagged [[cheerp::genericjs]] compiles to JavaScript and can call DOM and JS APIs directly through the client namespace (<cheerp/clientlib.h>), and [[cheerp::jsexport]] exposes C++ functions and whole classes to handwritten JavaScript. It is not a drop-in emcc replacement: flags, runtime, libc (musl + dlmalloc since 3.0) and the JS loading model differ, and the build-from-source path spans four repos (cheerp-compiler, cheerp-musl, cheerp-utils, cheerp-libs).
how_it_is_fast: Cheerp keeps LLVM bitcode as the object and library format and internalizes every definition at link time, so whole-program LTO, a devirtualizer, identical code folding, PreExecuter (runs global constructors at compile time) and PartialExecuter (drops code proven unreachable from known arguments) run before codegen. Its own CFGStackifier (successor to a Relooper) and Registerize (locals allocator) emit final WebAssembly in one step, with no Binaryen wasm-opt post-pass. The vendor credits these mainly with smaller output; for run time the 2023 post claims only parity with Emscripten.
when_to_use: C++ libraries that must live inside a JavaScript/TypeScript web app and call DOM or JS APIs directly, where Emscripten's embind/EM_JS glue is the pain point.
Projects that want part of the code as plain JavaScript ([[cheerp::genericjs]], garbage-collected objects) and the hot part in linear-memory WebAssembly, from one C++ source.
Download-size-sensitive web builds, where the vendor reports about 7% smaller output than Emscripten 3.1.31 on Emscripten's own test suite.
Teams that want a single-step toolchain (no separate wasm-opt pass) under Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception, the same licence as upstream LLVM.
when_not_to_use: When run-time speed is the reason to switch: the newest vendor data (Cheerp 3.0 vs Emscripten 3.1.31) claims execution 'comparable' to Emscripten, and no independent measurement shows Cheerp faster.

Multithreaded code (pthreads, WebAssembly atomics): missing in the last tagged release, cheerp-3.0; thread and atomics work exists only on the master branch (libthreads.bc, a sharedmem feature flag, CheerpOS threads), with no tag after March 2023.

Large ports that rely on Emscripten's ecosystem: virtual filesystem, SDL/GL ports, emscripten ports and wide community support; Cheerp issue #76 (2018) showed several Emscripten benchmark programs failing or not building under Cheerp, though that predates 2.0.

Type-unsafe C (custom pool allocators, qsort/bsearch/memcmp on untyped memory) in the JavaScript (genericjs) target, which maps C++ objects to JS objects and rejects such code; the wasm target does not have this restriction.

integration.form: compiler toolchain (prebuilt: Debian/Ubuntu PPA per the 3.0 post, an npm 'cheerp' package per the cheerp-meta badge, a macOS DMG built in CI; or build from source)
integration.dependencies: cheerp-compiler (LLVM/Clang fork) plus cheerp-musl, cheerp-utils and cheerp-libs (libc++/libc++abi built twice, for genericjs and wasm)
integration.min_toolchain: Building from source: CMake and Ninja, with LLVM built with -DCLANG_ENABLE_OPAQUE_POINTERS=OFF; Cheerp 3.0 is rebased on LLVM/Clang 16. Compiled code: most of C++20 (all of it in WebAssembly mode per the FAQ draft).
integration.platforms: Output runs in browsers (V8, SpiderMonkey, JavaScriptCore) and Node, or in WASI runtimes such as Wasmtime for -target cheerp-wasm-wasi; WebAssembly SIMD supported since 3.0
integration.thread_safety: Single-threaded output in the tagged 3.0 release (WebAssembly atomics and multithreading listed as the missing feature); Web Workers can be used as separate instances
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: clang-compatible command line, but it replaces emcc with different flags, runtime, JS loader, libc and interop attributes, and some Emscripten-specific APIs and ports have no equivalent

gotchas: The speed claim is shaky and vendor-only: snippets of the 2.6rc1 post (December 2020, Box2D, Bullet, zlib and LZMA against Emscripten 2.0.9 on V8 and SpiderMonkey, mean of three runs) give about 5% faster and about 3% smaller, but the Cheerp 3.0 post (March 2023, readable in leaningtech/labs) claims only 7% smaller output and 'comparable' execution against Emscripten 3.1.31; its data sits in Google Sheets and leaningtech.com SVG charts that could not be opened here, and no CPU, flags or per-benchmark numbers are given.

Past vendor comparisons have needed correction by Emscripten's author: issue #8 (2016) found the Cheerp 1.2 '10x faster startup' figure timed from the first executed line to main(), excluding parsing (about 15 ms of the real startup), and the real gap was up to about 2x; issue #76 (2018) found Emscripten 1.37.36 output 23-43% smaller than Cheerp where Cheerp's site claimed 30% smaller, until benchmarks were edited to drop printf.

Docs drift: the docs badge and changelog stop at 3.0 while master has gained threads, resizable memory and CheerpOS work; the draft porting guide still says exceptions are unsupported (they are opt-in with -fexceptions since 2.7); the default linear heap size is given as 1 MB on the targets page and 8 MB on the -cheerp-linear-heap-size page.
C++ exceptions are opt-in (-fexceptions), unlike native compilers, and the -cheerp-avoid-wasm-traps flag is needed to stop float-to-int conversions from trapping.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Among the catalogued wasm entries it is, with the msf/wasmplay Zig build, one of only two whose baseline is Emscripten itself; pick Cheerp when C++ must interoperate tightly with JavaScript and the DOM or ship as smaller output, not for speed, since the wasmplay Zig build reports a measured 1.29x win over em++ while Cheerp claims parity.
verified_claims_summary: Only first-party numbers exist: Leaning Technologies benchmarked Cheerp 2.6rc1 against Emscripten 2.0.9 on Emscripten's suite (Box2D, Bullet, zlib, LZMA) on one MacBook Pro running Linux with TurboBoost off, mean of three runs, and reported about 5% faster and 3% smaller output (search snippets only); the Cheerp 3.0 post against Emscripten 3.1.31 reports 7% smaller output and execution comparable on V8, SpiderMonkey and JavaScriptCore, with no CPU model or flags.
status_note: Actively developed by Leaning Technologies (last commit 2026-10-09, used to build CheerpJ, CheerpX and WebVM) and Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception since 3.0, but the last tagged release is cheerp-3.0 from March 2023, so new features such as threads are master-only.
